title: Copilot code-review findings lead with the fix, then a Why section
answers: How should Copilot review comments be formatted?
What order should review findings use: fix or explanation first?
Where is the code review comment format defined for Copilot?
How do I change the wording or structure of automated PR review comments?
body:
Convention: each review finding is written as two bolded sections, "**🔧 Fix:**" first (the recommended change, with only the detail needed to implement it), then "**💡 Why:**" (the trigger and concrete consequence).
Where: .github/instructions/code-review.instructions.md, section "## Review Comment Format", which is read by the Copilot code reviewer.
Keep the fix leading. Do not move the rationale above it or add a free-form preamble, or the reviewer output stops matching this format.
When editing this file, keep the section ahead of "## Knowledge Cutoff" and preserve the two labels exactly, since they are the format's contract.
The format applies to findings that come with a fix; the text does not define a format for comments without one.
applies: Edits to .github/instructions/code-review.instructions.md and the format of Copilot-generated PR review comments in this repo.
says: Automated pull request review comments should show the suggested fix before the explanation.
Make automated code review findings lead directly with the solution followed by the rationale.
Automated reviewer comments put lengthy explanations ahead of the code change recommendation.
Remove conversational intro text from automated review comments and start with the fix.
Automated pull request review findings are missing standard fix and why section headings.
search: Copilot code-review findings with fixes must be structured with **🔧 Fix:** first followed by **💡 Why:**. Defined in .github/instructions/code-review.instructions.md under ## Review Comment Format, this convention forbids moving rationale above the fix or adding a free-form preamble. When modifying the file, preserve the two exact labels and keep the section positioned ahead of ## Knowledge Cutoff. The format governs only review findings that include a fix, with comments lacking fixes left undefined.
